# Policy-KB bijection audit — autopay_authorization_changes / task 0

Scope: extended policies `autopay_ext_parking_draft_notice` (root), `autopay_ext_parking_ach_catchup`, `autopay_ext_unit_card_catchup`; the base policies they reference (`autopay_evt_varying_amount_notice`, `autopay_evt_expiry_reminders`, `autopay_evt_draft_amount_timing`, `autopay_evt_retry_and_suspension`, `autopay_evt_returns`) plus the remaining base policies of the charter for the retired surface and the reverse scan; variant parameters of the six AutoPay methods; the parking and unit class figures the factors read (checked against `blueprint/products/parking.yaml` and `unit.yaml` variants); task-tool contracts in `task_tools.py`. Corpus: 51 `docs/autopay/*.json` (title/content). Audited 2026-10-10 after the runtime blind audit (`runtime_context/autopay_authorization_changes/0.md`) was frozen.

## bijection_verdict
**PASS** — every atom of the three extended policies (baseline, every tier of every declared factor, both prerequisites, both overwrites) and of the base policies is carried at the same strength; no KB claim lacks a source. First revision; no previous revisions.

Policy-side notes (recorded, not KB defects):
- N1: `task_tools.py` docstring of `approve_card_catchup_charge_edda4662` reads "for a rent due date whose card draft is still declined after its retries", while the source rule says the catch-up may be approved "whether or not its retries are used" (the KB follows the rule; its tool block omits the docstring's qualifier). The runtime tool schema therefore states a narrower scope than the policy. Not triggered here (retries used).
- N2: the catch-up rules' prose defines the in-flight draft as "a regular draft … for a later due date whose result is still empty", while the compute reads only the latest-dated draft; the KB renders the compute reading. Differs only if a later-dated re-presentment were pending while an earlier-dated regular later-due draft is also pending.
- N3: variant parameter `draft_amount_basis: full_balance_due` remains in the variants and is rendered in the rate sheet ("Amount basis on the schedule: full balance due") although the base clause that gave it meaning is retired by the notice policies' overwrite; the KB retires the clause and keeps the parameter, exactly as the source does.
